misconception_description: Student believes that modifying a for loop variable inside the loop body does not affects the next iteration's value.

solutions.generated_code:
program JumlahMinMaks
kamus
  n, i, x, minimum, maksimum : integer
algoritma
  input(n)
  for i <- 1 to n do
    input(x)
    if i == 1 then
      minimum <- x
      maksimum <- x
    else
      if x < minimum then
        minimum <- x
      endif
      if x > maksimum then
        maksimum <- x
      endif
    endif
    i <- i + 2
  endfor
  output(minimum + maksimum)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrites the solution using a manual loop to find max and min values. They add `i += 2` at the end of each iteration, believing this will make the loop skip every other element to process the array faster. From their perspective, this seems like an optimization. However, the `i` modification has no effect on the loop's progression since `range(len(nums))` controls the iteration. Despite this misunderstanding, the code still functions correctly and produces the right output because all elements are still examined - the loop variable modification is simply ignored. The student genuinely believes they've made the code more efficient by "checking every other element" but in reality all elements are still processed.
